display.purpose: Hero headline. One per page. Clamp max 4.5rem, deliberately under the shouting threshold.

headline.purpose: Section headings. The workhorse level; most h2 elements use it.

body.purpose: List items and standard copy. Cap at 65-75ch.

label.purpose: Uppercase status labels only. 0.08em tracking lifted from the wordmark's WORKFORCE line. Never a section eyebrow.

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: Light-surface documents and print only. Unused on the website.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: The primary amber button. The only shadow appearing in normal page flow.

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: Overlaid surfaces: the mobile navigation panel. Signals 'above the page'.

shadows.name: glow-amber
shadows.purpose: Atmospheric hero glow. Never attached to a card as elevation.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Micro-feedback: icon colour shifts, small state flips.

motion.name: dur-base
motion.purpose: Default for hover and focus transitions on buttons, links and nav.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The single brand curve. CSS transitions and the JS Reveal component share it so motion feels like one system.

motion.name: reveal
motion.value: opacity 0 to 1, translateY 20px to 0 over 500ms on ease-out, once, at 20% in view
motion.purpose: The page's only scroll motion. Gives each section a beat. Fully suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Signature Brand Surface
components.description: The brand's own texture: a 40px amber grid at 5% over Ink Teal, plus an off-centre amber radial. Reserved for moments that must feel like the brand rather than like a section.

narrative.overview:
This system borrows its logic from safety-wear, not from web design. On a working site, one colour is reserved for the thing that must be seen, and everything else deliberately recedes so that reservation still means something at the end of a long shift. Hi-Vis Amber is that colour here. Ink Teal is everything else: the ground, the panels, the bands, the dark you read against. The discipline is not 'use amber sparingly for taste' - it is that amber marks the next action, and if two ambers compete in one viewport, one of them is a bug.

The surface is dark end to end, and that is a locked decision rather than a mood. The brand mark is an Ink Teal wordmark with amber chevrons; the tokens are built on dark surfaces shared across the Maintain group. A section that flips to a light theme mid-scroll breaks the family resemblance, so it does not happen. Depth is carried by 1px hairlines at 10% white and by tonal steps between Ink Teal, near-black and panel-black - not by shadow. Shadow is reserved for things that are genuinely lifted off the page.

What this system explicitly rejects: editorial-magazine styling - display-serif italic headlines, ruled multi-column grids, tracked lowercase metadata, and layouts where typography carries the entire visual weight. This brand has hi-vis and real crews in it; it is not a type specimen. Manrope carries every level, and contrast comes from weight and size, never from a borrowed second family.
keyCharacteristics: One accent, rationed. Amber is a signal, not a decoration.
Dark-locked surface, no theme flips between sections.
Flat at rest; hairlines and tonal steps do the work shadows usually do.
One type family (Manrope), 400 through 800, doing all the talking.
Status is always a dot plus a written label, never colour alone.
Field-legible: large tap targets, high contrast, no hover-only meaning.

rules.name: The Hi-Vis Rule
rules.body: Amber marks the next action. One primary amber element per viewport. If a second one appears, demote it to a ghost button or a hairline border - do not 'balance' the composition by adding more amber.

rules.name: The Dark Lock Rule
rules.body: The page background is Ink Teal from header to footer. Sections change texture - grid overlay, glow, terrain photograph, near-black band - never mode. No section is permitted to introduce a light theme.

rules.name: The Dot-and-Label Rule
rules.body: A status is a coloured dot plus a neutral uppercase label. Colour never carries the meaning on its own. This holds for colour-blind users and it holds for the accent budget; both reasons are load-bearing.

rules.name: The Single Family Rule
rules.body: Manrope carries every level. Hierarchy comes from weight (800 vs 400) and size, never from importing a second family. A display serif on this brand is a costume.

rules.name: The Caps-For-Labels-Only Rule
rules.body: Uppercase with 0.08em tracking is reserved for short status labels and the wordmark. It is explicitly not available as a section eyebrow. Never set body copy in caps.

rules.name: The Balance Rule
rules.body: text-wrap: balance on h1-h3, text-wrap: pretty on long prose. Headings this large produce ugly orphans without it.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Reach for the hairline first, the tonal step second, and a shadow only when neither can express the relationship.

rules.name: The Lift-Means-Action Rule
rules.body: A shadow means interactive or overlaid. A static informational panel never carries one.

dos: Do spend amber on the next action and nothing else. One primary amber element per viewport.
Do use Amber Deep (#8F6400) when amber must be text on a light surface. Hi-Vis Amber (#FFC400) fails contrast as text on white.
Do keep every border at 1px hairline (10% white) on all four sides.
Do express depth as hairline first, tonal step second, shadow last.
Do pair every status colour with a written uppercase label.
Do hold body copy to 65-75ch and lead paragraphs to ~58ch.
Do give every animation a prefers-reduced-motion alternative. tokens.css ships the global block; component motion must honour it too.
Do keep tap targets at 44x44px or larger, and keep all meaning available without hover.
Do reach for the platform first - <details> for disclosure, <dialog> for modals - before adding a client component.
donts: Don't use editorial-magazine styling: no display-serif italic headlines, no ruled multi-column grids, no tracked lowercase metadata, no layouts where typography carries the entire visual weight. Named in PRODUCT.md as the anti-reference.
Don't build a hero-metric template - big number, small label, supporting stats row.
Don't ship identical icon/heading/text card grids repeated down the page.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text). One solid colour; emphasis via weight or size.
Don't use glassmorphism as decoration. The header's backdrop blur is functional (content scrolls beneath it); nothing else gets one.
Don't use a coloured side-stripe border - no border-left over 1px as an accent.
Don't put a tiny tracked uppercase eyebrow above every section. Caps are for status labels and the wordmark only.
Don't flip a section to a light theme. The page is dark from header to footer.
Don't introduce a second font family, an icon library, or a colour outside this file.
Don't attach the amber glow to a card. It is atmosphere, not elevation.
Don't let a status read by colour alone.
